prompt_text:
You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw.

## Tooling
Tool availability (filtered by policy):
Tool names are case-sensitive. Call tools exactly as listed.
- todo_create_task: Create a new todo task
- todo_list_tasks: List todo tasks
When a first-class tool exists for an action, use the tool directly.

## Tool Schemas
Complete JSON Schema for available tools:
- todo_create_task
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "title": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "description": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "priority": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "due_date": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "title"
  ]
}
```
- todo_list_tasks
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "status": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": []
}
```

## Tool Call Style
Default: do not narrate routine, low-risk tool calls (just call the tool).
Narrate only when it helps: multi-step work, complex tasks, or sensitive actions.
Keep narration brief and value-dense.
Tool-call protocol is strict: use native API tool/function calls only.
Never emit tool calls as plain text markup (for example: <tool_call>, <function=...>, <parameter=...>).
If a tool is needed, issue a real tool call block instead of describing or simulating it in text.

## Safety
- Safety: No independent objective; do not pursue self-preservation, replication, or resource acquisition.
- Tool Call Style: For low-risk actions, call tools directly without narration; narrate only for complex tasks.
- Reply Tags: Use [[reply_to_current]] to control reply relationship when needed.
- Silent Reply: If no reply is needed, output NO_REPLY.
- Heartbeat: Heartbeat checks should return HEARTBEAT_OK when no action is needed.

## Skills (mandatory)
Before replying: scan <available_skills> entries.
- If exactly one skill clearly applies: read its SKILL.md using the configured read tool, then follow it.
- If multiple skills could apply: choose the most specific one, then read and follow it.
- If none clearly apply: do not read any SKILL.md.
Constraints: never read more than one skill up front; only read after selecting.
The full SKILL.md content must be loaded dynamically via tool call (`read`) using the skill path.
<available_skills>
</available_skills>

## Workspace Files (injected)

content.text:
Instead of creating files directly, use the todo service to bootstrap a Python
library project plan for "datautils". Create actionable tasks for:
1. creating the package structure under src/datautils
2. adding tests
3. writing pyproject metadata
4. writing a README
Then summarize the setup plan.

input.title: Create datautils package directory
input.description: Create `src/` and add `datautils/` module skeleton (e.g., `__init__.py`, placeholder modules/functions).

input.title: Add unit tests
input.description: Write unit tests for core functionality in `src/datautils/__init__.py` and/or other modules.

input.title: Add integration tests (optional)
input.description: Write integration tests that cover how the library works end-to-end (if applicable).

input.title: Configure test runner
input.description: Set up pytest (or equivalent) as the default test runner and ensure tests pass locally.

input.title: Write pyproject.toml metadata
input.description: Add `[tool.setuptools]` section including version, author, description, license, classifiers, entry points if any, and dependencies.

input.title: Add CI configuration
input.description: Add GitHub Actions (or similar) workflow for testing on push/pull request and optionally coverage reporting.

input.title: Write README
input.description: Create `README.md` explaining what the library does, installation steps, usage examples, and links to documentation/tests.

input.title: Document API
input.description: Add docstrings to key functions/classes and generate/update Sphinx/API docs (optional but recommended).

input.title: Add linting/formatting
input.description: Integrate black/isort/flake8/pydocstyle (or equivalent) and configure `.pre-commit-config.yaml` for automatic formatting/linting.

input.title: Add type hints
input.description: Add type annotations to all public APIs and update stubs if necessary.

input.title: Add coverage reporting
input.description: Enable code coverage measurement and report (e.g., codecov), ensuring meaningful coverage goals.

I’ve created **actionable todo tasks** to bootstrap your **Python library project “datautils”**, avoiding direct file creation until you’re ready to implement.

---

## Setup Plan Summary (Tasks Created)
### 1) Package Structure
- **todo_001**: Create `src/` and add `datautils/` module skeleton (`__init__.py`, placeholders).

### 2) Tests
- **todo_002**: Add unit tests for core functionality.
- **todo_003**: Add optional integration tests (end-to-end).
- **todo_004**: Configure test runner (pytest/equivalent) and ensure local success.

### 3) Metadata & Build
- **todo_005**: Write `pyproject.toml` metadata (`[tool.setuptools]` + version/author/description/license/classifiers/entrypoints/dependencies).

### 4) Documentation
- **todo_007**: Write `README.md` (what it does, install, usage, links to docs/tests).
- **todo_008**: Document API (add docstrings to key functions/classes; optional Sphinx/docs).

### 5) Quality & Maintenance
- **todo_009**: Add linting/formatting (black/isort/flake8/pydocstyle) + pre-commit config.
- **todo_010**: Add type hints to public APIs (and update stubs if needed).

### 6) Coverage & CI
- **todo_011**: Enable code coverage reporting (codecov/etc.) with meaningful goals.
- **todo_006**: Add CI configuration (GitHub Actions/workflow for PR/push + optional coverage).

---

Let me know if you’d like me to also create the actual initial files (e.g., `src/datautils/__init__.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `README.md`) once we agree on the scope!
